page: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 16-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. Storage includes a bundled 944 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem throughput. The PassMark memory test places this instance in the top 10 percent, supported by uncached large-block read bandwidth of 304.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 123.05 GB/sec. General compute metrics, including Geekbench multi-core at 14685.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 33147.69, fall into the middle 50 percent category. Single-threaded gzip compression demonstrates strong results at 33.05 GB/sec, whereas LLM prompt processing for 7B models falls into the bottom quartile at 24.6 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated vector acceleration units found on specialized platforms.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio combined with dedicated non-hyperthreaded ARM cores delivers consistent memory density and execution stability. Bundling high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external disk latency for high-frequency disk-buffered operations. These characteristics make the E16pds_v6 well suited for in-memory databases such as Redis, relational database management systems, data decompression pipelines, and caching infrastructure.
